newsitem.title: UK: Fund industry says MGAM moves inevitable.
newsitem.headline: Fund industry says MGAM moves inevitable.

text.p: The departure of four directors from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), following an internal probe into irregularities at three of its funds was inevitable but the changes will not necessarily restore confidence, fund management industry sources said on Wednesday.
Earlier Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, said MGAM's chief executive Keith Percy was leaving the firm along with three key managers.
Percy is the highest level casualty of the debacle, which began last month with the temporary suspension of the funds and led to the dismissal of former star fund manager Peter Young.

The problems at MGAM, which centred on the holding of unquoted stocks held in the MG European Growth Trust, MG Europa Fund and MG European Capital Growth Fund, have brought into focus the whole question of managerial responsibility.
"This is accepted as being a reason to look very seriously indeed at the management side of the business," one industry souce, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

He said the fact that MGAM's chief investment officer Glyn Owen, the head of the unit trust business Graham Kane and the head of compliance Mike Wheatley were all leaving the firm as well as Percy was symptomatic of the growing trend.
"Most people will think it fairly reasonable that the chap in charge of the firm, who is paid a lot of money, should be responsible. Everyone must acknowledge that," he added.

Some banking sources questioned whether DMG had achieved its aim of restoring its reputation in the unit trust business, adding there were still questions over reporting lines being transferred back to Frankfurt rather than London.

A likely solution was for the retail asset management portion of MGAM's 70 billion stg funds under management to be moved to Frankfurt, leaving the bulk under London's control, one banking source told Reuters.

A DMG spokesman said it was too early to say who would replace Owen, Wheatley, Kane and Paul Ebling, a senior associate director who is also leaving. Percy's replacement was earlier confirmed as Robert Smith, who moves from his position as head of Morgan Grenfell Development Capital.
"There is nothing to add (to an earlier statement) at the moment. This is up to the new management," he said.

When the problems at MGAM first arose, Deutsche immediately injected 180 million stg in cash to shore up the funds and subsequently said it would buy units in the funds to ensure liquidity and protect investors' interests.
This was seen as crucial in ensuring the fund management arm's reputation was not damaged beyond repair.
Deutsche has acted to limit the fall-out from the affair, fearful that it will reflect badly on its aggressive push into London's investment banking arena.

Young, fund manager of two of the funds currently being probed by British investment watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) is under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO). He has denied any criminal activity and said he was being made a scapegoat for internal failings.
The IMRO inquiry, which Morgan Grenfell says it will continue to cooperate with now that its own probe is "largely complete", is not expected to be finalised for some months.
If it finds MGAM has breached its rules it could impose hefty fines and take action against individuals.
